claims.text: The starting material is a eutectic high-entropy alloy with a hierarchical microstructure of dual-phase lamellar colonies.
Ion irradiation can introduce a controlled amount of lattice distortion into the starting alloy.
Irradiation-induced lattice distortion will reduce dislocation pile-ups near internal boundaries.
Reducing dislocation pile-ups will reduce local stress concentrations near internal boundaries.
Ion irradiation will improve room-temperature tensile ductility relative to the untreated starting material.
Ion irradiation will retain or increase strength relative to the untreated starting material.
Heterogeneous or multiphase high-entropy alloys can exhibit favorable strength–ductility combinations.
In a nano-lamellar AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy, the B2 phase is harder than the L12 phase and can eventually deform as room-temperature deformation increases.
The proposed effect is applicable to eutectic high-entropy alloys with similar microstructures.
The proposed evaluation should use room-temperature tensile testing.
The untreated starting material is the baseline for strength and ductility comparisons.
Ion irradiation may affect corrosion resistance or high-temperature strength.
The hypothesis can be tested by comparing tensile strength and ductility in samples with and without controlled lattice distortion.
